concerns.text: The table states T009 (manifest) 'executes unconditionally' if the amendment is rejected, but T009 is ordered 'after T004–T008' and its specified content (descriptors, PC scores, exclusion flags from T003/T004) cannot exist without the amendment-contingent tasks. As written, T009 is unexecutable in the rejection path; either define the reduced rejection-path manifest artifact explicitly or remove the 'unconditional' claim.

T009 requires manifest.csv validated against manifest.schema.yaml, but the schema has nested object fields (pc_scores, fdr_p_values as mappings) that cannot be plain CSV columns. The task never specifies the CSV encoding of these nested structures (JSON-string cells? separate columns?), so 'pytest tests/test_manifest.py asserts the manifest is syntactically valid' is not deterministically executable. Name the encoding convention.

T006 computes 'required N ... via statsmodels.stats.power' but never names the target power value (FR-010's is [deferred] and nothing fills it in). Without a stated power (e.g. 0.80) the required-N computation — and its pytest check 'against a known statsmodels reference value' — is under-specified; the implementer cannot pick the reference value deterministically.

T003's fallback 'else documented amplitude-based scrubbing' names no threshold or rule (the spec edge case is FD > 0.5 mm for >20% of volumes). On the expected no-FD-column path, the >20%-bad-volume exclusion rule has no defined 'bad volume' criterion, so the edge-case verification ('subjects with >20% bad volumes are flagged') is not executable as specified. State the amplitude-based bad-volume definition (e.g. DVARS-like threshold) in the task or config.

T003 says 'Peak memory stays under 7 GB (row-group streaming; verified in T011)' but T011 is the research.md writing task; peak RAM is recorded in T010's results/performance_metrics.txt. Fix the cross-reference so the verification points at the task that actually measures it.
T010–T012 carry '[P?]' priority placeholders; assign concrete priorities so scheduling/routing is deterministic.
